title: BUILD MIXED
subtitle: 12-Week Functional Fitness Programme
description: A progressive mixed-model programme that develops strength, muscle, skill, aerobic fitness and varied functional-fitness conditioning through explicit RX and Scaled prescriptions.
intended_athlete: Adults with basic gym experience who can train five core days per week and have access to a functional-fitness gym or suitable substitutions.

foundation.title: The programme in one page
foundation.summary: Broad fitness, structured progression and a reason behind every session.

sections.title: The outcome
points: Stronger squat, hinge, press and pull patterns.
More useful muscle and better local strength endurance.
Improved gymnastics, rope and weightlifting skill.
A larger aerobic base and more repeatable hard intervals.
Better pacing, transitions and execution across varied mixed-modal workouts.

sections.title: The commitment
points: Five core sessions each week: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday and Saturday.
Thursday is a rest day. Sunday recovery and education is optional.
Most sessions take 60-75 minutes. Deload weeks intentionally do less.
Full completion is five core sessions; optional work is reported separately.

foundation.coach_rule: The work changes, but the progression does not. Variety serves strength, skill, engine or execution - it is never random punishment.

foundation.title: Run the plan without guessing
foundation.summary: Read the session purpose and target before looking at the score.

sections.title: Before training
points: Rate readiness honestly.
Select RX or Scaled for this workout.
Check equipment, movement standards, cap and target.
Warm up the exact patterns and rehearse one short piece at workout pace.

sections.title: During training
points: Strength work stops before technical failure.
Skill practice stops when timing or position changes.
Use planned breaks and repeatable opening pace.
A cap ends the workout; it is not permission to ignore mechanics.

sections.title: After training
points: Record the track, exact load, movement changes and score.
Log interval or round splits when requested.
Name the first limiter and one next decision.
Normal training soreness should improve; pain that changes movement needs action.

foundation.coach_rule: If a core session is missed, continue the week. Do not double hard sessions, sacrifice the deload or turn the optional day into punishment.

foundation.title: Weekly structure and progression
foundation.summary: Hard work is separated so quality can survive; overload is followed by planned recovery.

sections.title: Move the days, keep the order
points: You may shift sessions to suit life, but preserve the sequence.
Avoid placing the two mixed conditioning days back-to-back with no recovery.
When life is compressed, prioritise Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Saturday.
Return to the normal structure next week; do not add missed volume later.

sections.title: What progression looks like
points: Strength: fewer repetitions and more load across each block, governed by RPE and clean mechanics.
Hypertrophy: repeatable sets with 1-3 good repetitions in reserve, not failure chasing.
Skill: positions first, then density, then controlled skill under fatigue.
Engine: stable aerobic intervals before threshold and high-output repeaters.
Conditioning: varied formats and movement combinations with an intentional repeated benchmark.

foundation.coach_rule: Weeks 4 and 8 reduce stress so the next block can begin with quality. Adding random hard work defeats the design.

foundation.title: Start in the right place
foundation.summary: BUILD MIXED is scalable, but it is not an unsupervised introduction to every movement.

sections.title: Get coaching when
points: You are new to barbell squat, deadlift, Olympic-lift derivatives or kipping gymnastics.
You cannot select a pain-free movement option confidently.
You do not know how to use racks, collars, benches or machines safely.

sections.title: Choose a longer on-ramp when
points: Five training days repeatedly overwhelms recovery.
Thirty minutes of easy continuous activity is not yet available.
Basic squat, hinge, push and pull patterns remain painful or inconsistent.

foundation.coach_rule: Video, text and timers cannot replace competent in-person coaching for unfamiliar or high-skill lifts.

entry_gate: Can complete at least 30 minutes of continuous easy aerobic activity using an appropriate mode.
Can perform scalable squat, hinge, push, pull and carry patterns without pain that changes movement.
Can use the listed equipment safely or obtain appropriate coaching and substitutions.
Can protect at least one full rest day and avoid doubling missed hard sessions.

onboarding_sequence.title: Before Week 1
onboarding_sequence.behaviour: Render all four entry-gate statements in full and require an answer or acknowledgement for each. If an athlete cannot meet an item, show an on-ramp/coaching message and keep the item visible; do not silently skip it or present it as a medical diagnosis.

session_preflight.readiness_check: Ask for one readiness option before each core session and show its exact action. Pain that changes movement must never be treated as a normal training score.
session_preflight.logging_rule: Record the actual track, load, substitutions, result and requested splits rather than assuming the published prescription was completed.

weekly_education.source: Every Sunday optional session contains an education block.

weekly_education.completion_rule: Track lesson read/completed separately from optional workout completion. Reading a lesson does not mark the workout complete and skipping recovery does not hide the lesson.

rx_scaled_policy.rule: Choose RX only when the prescription preserves the stated stimulus, movement standard, target time and planned set size. Otherwise use Scaled and record the exact change.
rx_scaled_policy.progression_rule: Progress one variable at a time when possible: range/control, movement difficulty, load, repetitions or pace.
rx_scaled_policy.no_shame_copy: Scaled is coached training, not a failed version of RX.
choose_rx_when: Target time or cap is achievable.
The load will not force failure or long unplanned rests.
choose_scaled_when: A movement needs a progression or different range.
The RX load would destroy the intended pace.
The workout would exceed its time domain.
Pain, equipment or experience requires a different option.
record_truth: Select a track for every workout.
Record exact dumbbell, kettlebell and barbell loads.
Record movement, distance, calorie or target changes.
Repeat the same setup during benchmark comparisons when possible.
rx_scaled_policy.full_credit_rule: A properly scaled workout counts exactly like RX for programme completion. The achievement is training the intended quality, not protecting a label.

load_standards.selection_test: Prescribed set size and pace survive.

load_standards.scaled_reference: Load or variation preserving repetitions and mechanics

rx_scaled_policy.dumbbell_rule: 22.5/17.5 kg is the programme RX pair where written. It is not automatically correct for every dumbbell exercise or every athlete. The workout still has to look like the stated target.
rx_scaled_policy.sex_load_rule: Where male/female loads are published, use the athlete profile for the reference. The athlete may still scale to preserve mechanics and stimulus.

equipment.substitution_principle: Match the movement pattern, work time and intended stimulus; do not replace every unavailable machine with extra running if impact tolerance is limited.
equipment.machine_conversions: Use time or effort rather than claiming exact calorie equivalence between rower, SkiErg, bike and running.

substitutions.keep_the_same: Work interval and breathing demand; do not claim exact calorie equality.

substitutions.keep_the_same: Leg repetitions and approximate work time.

rpe_and_repetitions_in_reserve.summary: Percentages guide the start; execution decides the finish.

scale.feel: Very hard, no technical error allowed
scale.use: Final test ceiling only; not routine work.

rpe_and_repetitions_in_reserve.load_adjustment: If the first work set is already above the planned RPE, reduce load. If it is clearly below and technique is excellent, make a small increase. The percentage is not a command to grind.
rpe_and_repetitions_in_reserve.stop_rule: A missed strength or weightlifting rep ends the loading climb. Record the miss, reduce or stop, and protect the next session.

squat: Week 1 establishes a technical five-rep reference at RPE 8.
Volume develops through sixes and fives before heavier threes and doubles.
Week 12 repeats the reference at RPE 8-9 rather than forcing a true maximum.
press: Strict work means no knee dip or leg drive.
Upper-body pulling and hypertrophy balance pressing volume.
Stop before failure; slow, shortened reps do not build the intended quality.
hinge: Romanian deadlifts build position and muscle early.
Deadlift triples and doubles increase later without maximal attempts.
The trunk and hamstrings should work; back position should not unravel.

conditioning_formats.rule: Start at a pace you can repeat; know the score but protect the movement.
Select reps/load leaving the stated rest; reduce before minutes become impossible.
Use target and cap; planned breaks beat failure.
Record every output; the first effort must not ruin the last.
Break the biggest stations deliberately and understand the remaining work.
Control early transitions so the larger late sets remain productive.
Treat each score distinctly and use the prescribed rest.

progress.completion_rule: Core completion and optional completion are separate. Five core sessions is a full week.
progress.comparison_rule: Changing the machine, load, target, movement option or standard changes the test. Record every change and interpret the result honestly.
progress.multi_dimensional_rule: A similar score with cleaner repetitions, smaller split fade or a harder legitimate scale is progress even when total repetitions barely change.
weekly_review_questions: Which session produced the best quality work, and why?
Where did pace, mechanics or standards first fail?
Did the selected RX/Scaled options preserve the intended stimulus?
What changed in sleep, stress, soreness or pain?
What single decision will improve next week?
progress.next_block_rule: After Week 12 choose one strength priority, one skill priority and one conditioning priority. Do not try to maximise everything at once.

learn.title: What BUILD MIXED develops
learn.summary: Functional fitness is the ability to produce useful force, move your body well and sustain output across different tasks and time domains.
points: Strength raises the ceiling: squat, hinge, press and pull with progressive loading.
Hypertrophy supplies muscle and tissue capacity for future strength and repeated work.
Skill turns strength into efficient gymnastics, rope and weightlifting movement.
Aerobic work improves recovery between efforts; intervals improve repeatable high output.
Mixed conditioning teaches pacing, transitions and strength endurance without replacing focused training.

learn.title: RX and Scaled are tools
learn.summary: RX is a published challenge, not a judgement. Scale when RX would change the intended duration, set size, mechanics or safety.
points: Choose the track separately for every workout.
Preserve the movement pattern, time domain and planned rest before preserving a number on the screen.
If the target is unbroken, use a load you can keep unbroken with clean reps.
If a movement is not yet safe, use the listed progression and record it exactly.
Progress the scale over time: more range, harder movement, more load or more work - usually one variable at a time.

learn.title: Strength progression
learn.summary: Normal strength work builds through submaximal repetitions, not constant maximal testing.
points: Week 1 supplies repeatable five-rep references for the squat and strict press.
Percentages are guides; RPE and technique decide the final load.
Stop a set if depth, bracing, bar path or speed changes materially.
No routine missed repetitions. A clean rep at the planned effort is more useful than a grind.
Week 12 repeats the reference conditions to show progress without requiring a true 1RM.

learn.title: Muscle and strength endurance
learn.summary: Hypertrophy work builds muscle with controlled sets; strength endurance teaches that muscle to repeat work under fatigue.
points: Most accessory sets finish with 1-3 good repetitions available.
Add repetitions before load when technique is still developing.
In conditioning, break before failure and resume on a planned cue.
Local muscle burn is expected; joint pain or changing mechanics is not a target.

learn.title: Gymnastics skill
learn.summary: Strict capacity, stable positions and rhythm come before high-repetition kipping.
points: Use ring rows and bands to own the pull through a full repeatable range.
Build hanging trunk control before forcing toes-to-bar volume.
Learn rope rhythm with relaxed shoulders and small jumps.
Stop practice when timing deteriorates; poor repetitions rehearse poor skill.

learn.title: Weightlifting skill and safety
learn.summary: Olympic-lift derivatives train speed and coordination only when the athlete controls the positions.
points: Use an empty bar, dumbbells or medicine ball until setup, pull and catch are consistent.
Add load only while the bar remains close and the landing remains balanced.
A missed lift ends the loading climb for that day.
Seek in-person coaching if the movement is unfamiliar; the app cannot assess technique remotely.

learn.title: Conditioning formats
learn.summary: The format changes the decision, not just the clock.
points: AMRAP: accumulate sustainable work; do not sprint the opening minute.
EMOM: select work that leaves planned rest in every minute.
For time: move efficiently within the target and cap; the cap is part of the prescription.
Intervals: make outputs repeatable and use the rest deliberately.
Chipper or ladder: plan breaks before the largest sets and understand what remains.

learn.title: Time domains and stimulus
learn.summary: Different durations develop different problems: speed, tolerance, threshold and long-duration pacing.
points: Very short work is under five minutes; short is roughly five to ten.
Moderate work is roughly eleven to twenty minutes; long work extends beyond twenty.
Scaling should keep the athlete in the intended time domain.
A ten-minute workout taking twenty-five minutes is a different session, even if every load is technically RX.

learn.title: Pacing and transitions
learn.summary: A strong result comes from useful work per minute, not the fastest first minute.
points: Begin at a pace that feels repeatable; earn the right to accelerate.
Use planned set sizes and short breaks before failure.
Arrange equipment safely and know the next movement before you finish the current one.
Record round splits or interval outputs; large fades reveal pacing, load or skill problems.

learn.title: Concurrent training
learn.summary: Strength and endurance can improve together when hard work is organised and recovery is protected.
points: Focused strength precedes conditioning when strength quality is the priority.
Tuesday develops skill and engine without another heavy lifting day.
Thursday is free from core work before Friday and Saturday.
Easy recovery must remain easy; adding intensity can erase its purpose.

learn.title: Readiness and missed sessions
learn.summary: Modify a day before poor readiness turns one session into a damaged week.
points: Ready: complete the selected prescription.
Average: use the lower load and remove a small amount of accessory or conditioning volume.
Heavy: reduce strength load 5-10% and conditioning volume about 20%.
Do not cram missed hard sessions, double the following day or sacrifice the deload.
Pain that changes movement ends that exercise; choose a pain-free option or seek assessment.

learn.title: Recovery, food and hydration
learn.summary: Training creates the signal; sleep and sufficient food allow adaptation.
points: Protect a consistent sleep opportunity and routine.
Eat enough total energy and distribute protein across meals.
Use carbohydrate around demanding sessions according to preference and tolerance.
Begin hydrated and replace fluid according to conditions and sweat loss.
Supplements do not compensate for inadequate food, sleep or programming.

learn.title: Benchmarking honestly
learn.summary: A benchmark is useful only when the conditions and standards are recorded.
points: Repeat the same RX or Scaled version, equipment, machine settings and movement standards when possible.
Record exact load, rounds/reps, split drift, limiter and any changed variable.
Weeks 1, 6 and 12 repeat Mixed 12 intentionally; other conditioning changes to create broad fitness.
A better score with poorer range or different scaling is not a clean comparison.

learn.title: Pain and medical safety
learn.summary: This programme is education, not individual medical assessment.
points: Stop for chest pain, fainting, severe breathlessness, sudden neurological symptoms or another concerning acute symptom and seek urgent medical help.
Do not train through pain that changes mechanics or worsens set to set.
Return after injury, illness, pregnancy or a medical issue with appropriate professional guidance.
Use safe equipment, clear working space and competent spotting where required.

weeks.objective: Establish honest scores, clean positions and sustainable pacing.
weeks.intensity: Moderate; tests stop before technical failure.

sessions.title: Lower strength + Controlled burn
sessions.purpose: Develop squat strength and lower-body capacity without compromising movement quality.
sessions.intensity: Moderate; tests stop before technical failure.

blocks.name: Prepare
blocks.instruction: 8-10 minutes: 3 minutes easy machine; 2 rounds of 8 air squats, 8 glute bridges, 6 reverse lunges per side; then 3 progressive empty-bar squat sets.
blocks.standard: The first work set should feel prepared, not surprising.

blocks.name: Back squat
blocks.instruction: Build to 5 reps at RPE 8, then 2 x 5 at 90% of that load.
blocks.rx: Barbell back squat to consistent depth.
blocks.scaled: Front squat, goblet squat or box squat using the same set structure and RPE.
blocks.stimulus: All work sets completed without a miss.
blocks.standard: Brace before descent; use a depth and stance you can reproduce safely.

blocks.name: Posterior chain
blocks.instruction: Romanian deadlift 3 x 8 at RPE 6.
blocks.rx: Barbell prescription as written.
blocks.scaled: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift or kettlebell deadlift at the same RPE.
blocks.stimulus: Hamstrings and trunk loaded without back position changing.
blocks.standard: Move consistently and stop if pain changes the movement.

blocks.name: Controlled burn
blocks.instruction: AMRAP 10: 10 DB front squats, 8 lateral burpees over the dumbbell, 150 m row.
blocks.rx: 22.5/17.5 kg dumbbells (male/female); two dumbbells; two-foot burpee jump.
blocks.scaled: 15/10 kg dumbbells or a load that preserves the stated set size and pace; step over the dumbbell; 120 m row.
blocks.stimulus: 3-5 steady rounds; squats in one set and no sprint start.
blocks.standard: Meet the stated movement standard on every counted repetition.

sessions.coach_note: The strength work drives progression. The conditioning piece should not turn tomorrow into a recovery problem.

sessions.title: Strict pulling baseline + Run intervals
sessions.purpose: Build a transferable gymnastics skill, then improve aerobic power or repeatability.
sessions.intensity: Skill at RPE 5-7; engine according to the stated target.

blocks.name: Prepare
blocks.instruction: 8 minutes: easy machine or jog; ankle, calf and hip preparation; then 3 x 20 seconds at the first work pace with 40 seconds easy.
blocks.standard: The first work set should feel prepared, not surprising.

blocks.name: Strict pulling baseline
blocks.instruction: Practise before fatigue. Stop a set when timing, range or control changes.
blocks.rx: Accumulate 20 strict pull-ups in small clean sets; record largest unbroken set.
blocks.scaled: Use a band or ring row angle that allows 5-8 perfect repetitions.
blocks.stimulus: Clean repetitions with no grinders or failed attempts.
blocks.standard: The chosen option must preserve control and the intended range of motion.

blocks.name: Run intervals
blocks.instruction: Complete the prescribed intervals and record every split.
blocks.rx: 6 x 400 m at controlled 3 km effort; walk/jog 90 seconds.
blocks.scaled: 6 x 2 minutes run or run-walk; 90 seconds easy.
blocks.stimulus: Fastest-to-slowest split drift <=5%.
blocks.standard: The first interval sets a pace you can defend.

blocks.name: Downshift
blocks.instruction: 5-8 minutes easy movement, then calves, hips and lats as needed.
blocks.standard: Move consistently and stop if pain changes the movement.

sessions.coach_note: Do not turn skill practice into conditioning. Rest enough to learn, then respect the engine target.

sessions.title: Upper strength + Upper-body clock
sessions.purpose: Progress strict pressing and pulling strength, then apply it in a mixed format.
sessions.intensity: Moderate; tests stop before technical failure.

blocks.name: Prepare
blocks.instruction: 8-10 minutes: 3 minutes easy machine; 2 rounds of 8 scapular push-ups, 10 band pull-aparts, 8 ring rows; then 3 progressive press sets.
blocks.standard: The first work set should feel prepared, not surprising.

blocks.name: Strict press
blocks.instruction: Build to 5 strict reps at RPE 8, then 2 x 5 at 90% of that load.
blocks.rx: Standing barbell strict press; no leg drive.
blocks.scaled: Seated or standing dumbbell strict press using the same sets and RPE.
blocks.stimulus: No missed repetitions and no change from strict to push press.
blocks.standard: Ribs stay controlled and the bar finishes over the mid-foot.

blocks.name: Pull + hypertrophy
blocks.instruction: 3 sets each: 8-12 chest-supported rows and 8-12 push-ups or DB bench. Keep 2-3 good reps in reserve.
blocks.rx: Choose loads/angles that reach the rep range with 2-3 good reps left.
blocks.scaled: Use lighter dumbbells, elevated push-ups or an easier row angle.
blocks.stimulus: Accumulate quality upper-body muscle work without failure.
blocks.standard: Move consistently and stop if pain changes the movement.

blocks.name: Upper-body clock
blocks.instruction: EMOM 12: Minute 1: 8 DB push press. Minute 2: 10 ring rows. Minute 3: 30 double unders.
blocks.rx: 17.5/12.5 kg dumbbells; feet-elevated ring rows; double unders.
blocks.scaled: 10/7.5 kg dumbbells; upright ring rows; 60 single unders.
blocks.stimulus: Work completes by 40 seconds; shoulders remain controlled.
blocks.standard: Meet the stated movement standard on every counted repetition.

sessions.coach_note: Pressing failure has a high cost and little benefit here. Scale before repetitions become slow or short.

sessions.title: Hang power clean + Clean pull couplet
sessions.purpose: Develop safe, repeatable weightlifting mechanics and express power in a short-to-moderate workout.
sessions.intensity: Moderate; tests stop before technical failure.

blocks.name: Prepare
blocks.instruction: 10 minutes: easy machine, ankles/hips/shoulders, then barbell positions with a dowel or empty bar. Add load only after consistent catches.
blocks.standard: The first work set should feel prepared, not surprising.

blocks.name: Hang power clean
blocks.instruction: Every 90 seconds x 8: 3 hang power cleans at RPE 6; reset every rep.
blocks.rx: Use the barbell movement as written only when catches and positions are consistent.
blocks.scaled: Use a hang variation, high pull, medicine-ball clean or dumbbell option selected with a coach.
blocks.stimulus: Every repetition is technically repeatable; no misses.
blocks.standard: Stop adding load when the catch, bar path or landing changes.

blocks.name: Clean pull couplet
blocks.instruction: AMRAP 9: 6 hang power cleans, 8 box jump-overs.
blocks.rx: Barbell at 50/35 kg; 24/20 in box.
blocks.scaled: Barbell or two dumbbells allowing six unbroken reps; step-overs.
blocks.stimulus: 6-9 rounds; clean sets remain unbroken and transitions stay calm.
blocks.standard: Meet the stated movement standard on every counted repetition.

blocks.name: Accessory durability
blocks.instruction: 2 rounds: 10 single-leg Romanian deadlifts per side, 12 face pulls, 30-45 seconds side plank per side.
blocks.rx: Controlled dumbbell loading.
blocks.scaled: Bodyweight or supported variations.
blocks.stimulus: Easy-moderate trunk, hip and shoulder work.
blocks.standard: Move consistently and stop if pain changes the movement.

sessions.coach_note: The lifting practice comes first. A faster workout score never justifies unsafe barbell mechanics.

sessions.title: Benchmark: Mixed 12
sessions.purpose: Integrate engine, strength endurance, skills and transitions in a distinct functional-fitness format.
sessions.intensity: Moderate; tests stop before technical failure.

blocks.name: Prepare
blocks.instruction: 10 minutes: easy row/run, then two controlled rounds of the main movement patterns. Finish with one short rehearsal at workout pace.
blocks.standard: The first work set should feel prepared, not surprising.

blocks.name: Benchmark: Mixed 12
blocks.instruction: AMRAP 12: 250 m row, 8 DB thrusters with two 22.5/17.5 kg dumbbells (male/female), 8 lateral burpees over the dumbbells.
blocks.rx: 250 m row, 8 DB thrusters with two 22.5/17.5 kg dumbbells (male/female), 8 lateral burpees over the dumbbells.
blocks.scaled: 200 m row, 8 DB thrusters with two 15/10 kg dumbbells or a sustainable pair, 8 step-over or regular burpees.
blocks.stimulus: 3-5 rounds; record rounds, reps, tie-break after each row and exact load.
blocks.standard: Meet the stated movement standard on every counted repetition.

blocks.name: Cooldown + review
blocks.instruction: 8 minutes easy movement. Record opening pace, first limiter, transition errors, exact track/load and one decision for next time.
blocks.standard: Move consistently and stop if pain changes the movement.

sessions.title: Lower strength + Squat test flush
sessions.purpose: Develop squat strength and lower-body capacity without compromising movement quality.

blocks.name: Prepare
blocks.instruction: 8-10 minutes: 3 minutes easy machine; 2 rounds of 8 air squats, 8 glute bridges, 6 reverse lunges per side; then 3 progressive empty-bar squat sets.
blocks.standard: The first work set should feel prepared, not surprising.

blocks.name: Back squat
blocks.instruction: Repeat the Week 1 five-rep build. Stop at RPE 8-9; do not grind.
blocks.rx: Barbell back squat to consistent depth.
blocks.scaled: Front squat, goblet squat or box squat using the same set structure and RPE.
blocks.stimulus: All work sets completed without a miss.
blocks.standard: Brace before descent; use a depth and stance you can reproduce safely.

blocks.name: Posterior chain
blocks.instruction: Romanian deadlift 2 x 6 at RPE 5, then stop.
blocks.rx: Barbell prescription as written.
blocks.scaled: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift or kettlebell deadlift at the same RPE.
blocks.stimulus: Hamstrings and trunk loaded without back position changing.
blocks.standard: Move consistently and stop if pain changes the movement.

blocks.name: Squat test flush
blocks.instruction: EMOM 8: Minute 1: 8 light kettlebell swings. Minute 2: 8 easy box step-ups.
blocks.rx: 16/12 kg kettlebell; 20/16 in box.
blocks.scaled: Light kettlebell or unweighted hinge; low stable step.
blocks.stimulus: RPE 5 after the squat retest; leave recovered.
blocks.standard: Meet the stated movement standard on every counted repetition.

sessions.coach_note: The strength work drives progression. The conditioning piece should not turn tomorrow into a recovery problem.

sessions.title: Skill retest + Engine retest
sessions.purpose: Build a transferable gymnastics skill, then improve aerobic power or repeatability.
sessions.intensity: Skill at RPE 5-7; engine according to the stated target.

blocks.name: Prepare
blocks.instruction: 8 minutes: easy machine or jog; ankle, calf and hip preparation; then 3 x 20 seconds at the first work pace with 40 seconds easy.
blocks.standard: The first work set should feel prepared, not surprising.

blocks.name: Skill retest
blocks.instruction: Practise before fatigue. Stop a set when timing, range or control changes.
blocks.rx: Repeat the Week 1 strict pull-up test and Week 2 best double-under set after full recovery.
blocks.scaled: Repeat the same scaled pull and rope tests used earlier.
blocks.stimulus: Clean repetitions with no grinders or failed attempts.
blocks.standard: The chosen option must preserve control and the intended range of motion.

blocks.name: Engine retest
blocks.instruction: Complete the prescribed intervals and record every split.
blocks.rx: Repeat Week 1: 6 x 400 m with 90 seconds recovery.
blocks.scaled: Repeat the exact Week 1 scaled interval.
blocks.stimulus: Compare average and split drift.
blocks.standard: The first interval sets a pace you can defend.

blocks.name: Downshift
blocks.instruction: 5-8 minutes easy movement, then calves, hips and lats as needed.
blocks.standard: Move consistently and stop if pain changes the movement.

sessions.coach_note: Do not turn skill practice into conditioning. Rest enough to learn, then respect the engine target.

sessions.purpose: Progress strict pressing and pulling strength, then apply it in a mixed format.

blocks.name: Prepare
blocks.instruction: 8-10 minutes: 3 minutes easy machine; 2 rounds of 8 scapular push-ups, 10 band pull-aparts, 8 ring rows; then 3 progressive press sets.
blocks.standard: The first work set should feel prepared, not surprising.

blocks.name: Strict press
blocks.instruction: Repeat the Week 1 five-rep build. Stop at RPE 8-9; do not grind.
blocks.rx: Standing barbell strict press; no leg drive.
blocks.scaled: Seated or standing dumbbell strict press using the same sets and RPE.
blocks.stimulus: No missed repetitions and no change from strict to push press.
blocks.standard: Ribs stay controlled and the bar finishes over the mid-foot.

blocks.name: Pull + hypertrophy
blocks.instruction: 2 sets each: 8-12 chest-supported rows and 8-12 push-ups or DB bench. Keep 2-3 good reps in reserve.
blocks.rx: Choose loads/angles that reach the rep range with 2-3 good reps left.
blocks.scaled: Use lighter dumbbells, elevated push-ups or an easier row angle.
blocks.stimulus: Accumulate quality upper-body muscle work without failure.
blocks.standard: Move consistently and stop if pain changes the movement.

blocks.name: Press test finish
blocks.instruction: AMRAP 6: 6 light DB push press, 8 ring rows, 20 single unders.
blocks.rx: 12.5/7.5 kg dumbbells; challenging ring-row angle.
blocks.scaled: Light dumbbells; easier ring-row angle; 20 line hops or marches.
blocks.stimulus: Fast but technically clean after the press retest; RPE no higher than 7.
blocks.standard: Meet the stated movement standard on every counted repetition.

sessions.coach_note: Pressing failure has a high cost and little benefit here. Scale before repetitions become slow or short.

sessions.title: Technique primer + Primer triplet
sessions.purpose: Develop safe, repeatable weightlifting mechanics and express power in a short-to-moderate workout.

blocks.name: Prepare
blocks.instruction: 10 minutes: easy machine, ankles/hips/shoulders, then barbell positions with a dowel or empty bar. Add load only after consistent catches.
blocks.standard: The first work set should feel prepared, not surprising.

blocks.name: Technique primer
blocks.instruction: Every 2 minutes x 5: 2 light power cleans + 1 jerk at RPE 5.
blocks.rx: Use the barbell movement as written only when catches and positions are consistent.
blocks.scaled: Use a hang variation, high pull, medicine-ball clean or dumbbell option selected with a coach.
blocks.stimulus: Every repetition is technically repeatable; no misses.
blocks.standard: Stop adding load when the catch, bar path or landing changes.

blocks.name: Primer triplet
blocks.instruction: 3 rounds for quality - 9 minutes: 5 light power cleans, 6 box step-overs, 8 easy wall balls.
blocks.rx: 30/20 kg barbell; 20/16 in box; 6/4 kg ball.
blocks.scaled: PVC or light dumbbells; low step; air squats to target.
blocks.stimulus: RPE 5; finish wanting another round.
blocks.standard: Meet the stated movement standard on every counted repetition.

blocks.name: Accessory durability
blocks.instruction: 1 round: 10 single-leg Romanian deadlifts per side, 12 face pulls, 30-45 seconds side plank per side.
blocks.rx: Controlled dumbbell loading.
blocks.scaled: Bodyweight or supported variations.
blocks.stimulus: Easy-moderate trunk, hip and shoulder work.
blocks.standard: Move consistently and stop if pain changes the movement.

sessions.coach_note: The lifting practice comes first. A faster workout score never justifies unsafe barbell mechanics.
